Ukrainian drone strikes are causing power outages, fuel shortages and cuts in cellphone service in the peninsula. Russia seized Crimea when it first invaded Ukraine in 2014, but now its hold on the territory is being challenged. Russia maintained an iron grip on Crimea since seizing it from Ukraine in 2014. Many Russian civilians go there to enjoy the beaches. But now Ukraine is hitting Crimea hard, upending daily life. KYIV, Ukraine — The Black Sea peninsula of Crimea is normally packed in the summer with families enjoying beach vacations. But not this year, as Ukraine's relentless drone strikes make life increasingly miserable.

"Transportation is completely at a standstill. No gasoline, no fuel, no power. The stores are closed. The banks are closed. Nothing works at all. There's no water either," a Russian woman said on social media .

Crimea was the first place Russian leader Vladimir Putin seized when he initially invaded Ukraine in 2014. An estimated 1 million Russian troops and civilians have poured into the territory to make it more Russian and less Ukrainian. With the Russian influx, and the departure of many Ukrainians, Crimea's population is now estimated at around 2.5 million.
Ukraine has vowed to get Crimea back and carried out periodic drone strikes in recent years, with limited effect. But the campaign has ramped up dramatically in the past couple months.

Russian military facilities have been hit hard, especially in the northern part of Crimea. For civilians, a critical shortage of basic services keeps getting worse in a place that relies heavily on imports.

Robert Shageyev was described on Russian Telegram channels as ‌a former Ukrainian naval officer who switched allegiance to ‌Russia during Moscow’s annexation of Crimea in 2014 when he was commanding Ukraine’s only submarine, the Zaporizhzhia . Myrotvorets – a Ukrainian website keeping a database of people described as war criminals or ‌traitors – said Shageyev had been “liquidated”.

The attack took place in Sevastopol, the biggest city in Russian-annexed Crimea. ​The regional governor, Mikhail Razvozhayev, said a woman was arrested on suspicion of ⁠assassinating Shageyev on behalf of Ukrainian special services. State news agency TASS quoted the FSB security service as saying the arrested woman was ⁠a Russian national. There was no immediate comment ⁠from Ukraine. Separately, Razvozhayev said four Russian explosives experts and a security guard were killed in Sevastopol while trying to dispose of an explosive device.

A Russian drone attack on a passenger train killed two people , Ukrainian officials said. “Today in the Odesa region, the Russians once again destroyed an ordinary passenger train locomotive with a jet-powered drone. There were 340 people on the train,” said the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, on Thursday. “Whoever was operating that drone certainly could not have been unaware that the target was entirely civilian,” he added. The dead were the train’s engineer and assistant engineer, officials said.

article.title: Qatar denies Iran
article.description: The dispute centers on an incident during Iran’s attacks on a military base in Qatar amid a broader regional conflict. Tehran said two Su-24 fighter jets were hit by air defenses during the operation.
paragraphs: Summary The dispute centers on an incident during Iran’s attacks on a military base in Qatar amid a broader regional conflict. Tehran said two Su-24 fighter jets were hit by air defenses during the operation.

DOHA (Dunya News) - Qatar on Saturday rejected Iran’s claim that three Iranian fighter pilots were captured alive by Qatari forces after their aircraft went down during attacks on the country in March, calling the allegation misleading.

Majed Al Ansari, adviser to Qatar’s prime minister and spokesperson for the Foreign Ministry, said Doha “categorically” denied the claim and questioned why it was being raised now as diplomatic efforts continue to ease regional tensions.
Al Ansari said Qatari authorities established contact with the Iranian pilots after they violated Qatar’s airspace and the trajectory of the incoming attack had been confirmed.

He said Qatari forces followed established rules of engagement and attempted unsuccessfully to communicate with the pilots before taking measures to defend Qatari territory in accordance with international law.

article.title: Several Palestinians injured as settlers continue attacks in West Bank
paragraphs: Israeli settlers continued their assaults on Palestinians and their property in the occupied West Bank, injuring several people. Here are the details of some of these attacks, reported by Wafa.

• The settlers raided the village of al-Mughayyir, northeast of Ramallah, and the outskirts of the nearby town of Sinjil. Local Palestinian residents confronted the settlers in the Shaab al-Louz area. No injuries were reported.
• Palestinian vehicles came under settler attack in the Marj Sia plain east of al-Mughayyir, along the road leading to the nearby village of Abu Falah.
• Local sources told Wafa the settlers stormed the northern outskirts of Sinjil and released their livestock among residents' homes.
